content: 1. Tipranavir and Nisoldipine: Tipranavir increases nisoldipine levels by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Tipranavir and Norethindrone: Tipranavir raises norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of serious adverse effects. 3. Tipranavir and Nortriptyline: Tipranavir increases nortriptyline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Tipranavir and Olaparib: Tipranavir raises olaparib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute capsules with tablets. 5. Tipranavir and Oliceridine: Tipranavir increases oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, reduce oliceridine dosing frequency and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. Adjust doses as needed. 6. Tipranavir and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir: Tipranavir increases the levels of this combination therapy by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Tipranavir and Orlistat: Orlistat reduces tipranavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, potentially leading to loss of virological control in HIV-infected patients. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 8. Tipranavir and Osilodrostat: Tipranavir increases osilodrostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Tipranavir and Osimertinib: Tipranavir raises osimertinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse effects. 10. Tipranavir and Oxycodone: Tipranavir increases oxycodone levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose reduction may be warranted. 11. Tipranavir and Paclitaxel: Tipranavir raises paclitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tipranavir and Palbociclib: Tipranavir increases palbociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day if unavoidable. 13. Tipranavir and Paroxetine: Tipranavir increases paroxetine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Tipranavir and Pazopanib: Tipranavir raises pazopanib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Tipranavir and Pomalidomide: Tipranavir affects pomalidomide levels through CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Tipranavir and Ponatinib: Tipranavir increases ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ponatinib dose to 30 mg daily if co-administration is unavoidable. 17. Tipranavir and Rifabutin: Tipranavir increases rifabutin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Tipranavir and Rifampin: Rifampin reduces tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to loss of antiviral efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Tipranavir and Rivaroxaban: Tipranavir increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Tipranavir and Rosuvastatin: Tipranavir increases rosuvastatin levels, raising the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Do not exceed a rosuvastatin dose of 10 mg/day. 21. Tipranavir and Sildenafil: Tipranavir raises sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of priapism, hypotension, and other adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Tipranavir and Simvastatin: Tipranavir significantly increases simvastatin levels, leading to a high risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Tipranavir and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort reduces tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to loss of antiviral efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Tipranavir and Sofosbuvir: Tipranavir reduces sofosbuvir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein transport, potentially decreasing its therapeutic effect. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Tipranavir and Siponimod: Tipranavir increases siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and CYP2C9 inhibitors is not recommended. 26. Tipranavir and Sirolimus: Tipranavir raises sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Tipranavir and Ruxolitinib: Tipranavir increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ruxolitinib dose to 10 mg twice daily if co-administration is unavoidable. 28. Tipranavir and Salmeterol: Tipranavir increases salmeterol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Tipranavir and Saxagliptin: Tipranavir raises saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the saxagliptin dose to 5 mg/day when co-administered. 30. Tipranavir and Solifenacin: Tipranavir increases solifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Tipranavir and Sonidegib: Tipranavir raises sonidegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 32. Tipranavir and Sorafenib: Tipranavir increases sorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Tipranavir and Pomegranate/Grapefruit Juice: Patients should avoid pomegranate and grapefruit juice as they may interact with tipranavir metabolism. 34. Tipranavir and Rilpivirine: Tipranavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Tipranavir and Rimegepant: Tipranavir raises rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Tipranavir and Sitagliptin: Tipranavir may reduce sitagliptin efficacy due to insulin resistance. Monitor blood glucose levels closely. 37. Tipranavir and Sofpironium: Tipranavir increases sofprionium levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 38. Tipranavir and Quetiapine: Monitor for clinical response and adverse effects. 39. Tipranavir and Quinidine: Tipranavir significantly increases quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Tipranavir and Red Yeast Rice: Tipranavir increases the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis when combined with red yeast rice, which contains lovastatin-like compounds. Avoid co-administration. 41. Tipranavir and Regorafenib: Tipranavir increases regorafenib levels while reducing its active metabolites. Co-administration is contraindicated. 42. Tipranavir and Rifapentine: Rifapentine reduces tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 43. Tipranavir and Rosiglitazone: Tipranavir may reduce rosiglitazone efficacy due to insulin resistance. Monitor blood glucose levels closely. 44. Tipranavir and Rucaparib: Tipranavir increases rucaparib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates as clinically indicated. 45. Tipranavir and Stiripentol: Tipranavir increases stiripentol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. This summary highlights the critical interactions and necessary precautions when using tipranavir with other medications.
